advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that granting grounding/resolve.py and grounding/oracle.py full composition-root ownership (all composition-category reads) is intended, rather than scoping ownership to the specific drained symbols.
evidence: scripts/check_config_ownership.py:188-195: `_is_owned` returns True for ANY `_OWNER_COMPOSITION` access when `_is_composition_root(relpath)` is true — env-read, load_config, getattr, unresolved-env-read, and configurable-default all become owned
The removed whitelist rows were per-symbol (resolve.py REBAR_CTAGS_BIN + load_config; oracle.py load_config), so the replacement grant is strictly broader than what it replaces

oracle.py docstring at src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py:3-8 describes it as a 'thin facade' that 'adds no detection logic of its own, it only routes and filters' — not a genuine config-owning composition root
advisory.finding: Registering grounding/resolve.py and grounding/oracle.py as composition-root relpaths grants them ownership of the ENTIRE composition category (env-read, load_config, getattr-env, unresolved-env-read, configurable-default), not just the specific REBAR_CTAGS_BIN/load_config reads being drained. Any future ambient composition read added to these two files will pass the gate silently, a detection-surface regression versus the previous explicit per-symbol whitelist rows.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral assertion exercising the unbound REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH override branch (L188) to match the test's documented coverage.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout.py docstring: 'the op-cert key-path and principal deployment overrides are still honored'
The test body only sets `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` and asserts `opcert_principal(tmp_path) == "prod:eu"` — no assertion touches `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` / `opcert_key_path`
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:188 the REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH read (a separately drained whitelist row) has no behavioral regression assertion
advisory.finding: test_opcert_overrides_apply_when_unbound documents that it covers both the op-cert key-path and principal deployment overrides when unbound, but only asserts the REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID/principal path; the REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH override branch (the other read disposed in this slice) is not exercised.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral regression test that, with no signer bound, sets REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH to an existing path and asserts ensure_opcert_key returns it (and that a missing override raises OpcertKeyUnavailable).
evidence: Diff removed the whitelist row '_opcert_signing.py','REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH','_opcert_signing.py L188' and annotated L188 with '# read-via: credential-deployment-override'
_opcert_signing.py:188 `override = os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH")  # read-via: credential-deployment-override` inside ensure_opcert_key (def at L156)

test_opcert_overrides_apply_when_unbound only does `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID", "prod:eu"); assert opcert_principal(tmp_path) == "prod:eu"` — it never calls ensure_opcert_key nor sets REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH
Oracle docstring line 7: 'The op-cert key-path / principal deployment overrides still apply when UNBOUND' — the key-path half is unasserted
advisory.finding: The disposed REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH read (ensure_opcert_key, L188 — its LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS row was removed in this diff) has no behavioral regression test, despite the held-out oracle's stated contract #7 ('the op-cert key-path ... deployment overrides still apply when UNBOUND') and the header claim of 'behavioral preservation of every disposed read'. test_opcert_overrides_apply_when_unbound only asserts REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID via opcert_principal; the ensure_opcert_key key-path override branch is never exercised, so a regression in that disposed read would pass unnoticed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test calling ensure_opcert_key(tmp_path) with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH set to an existing file (asserting it is returned) and to a nonexistent path (asserting OpcertKeyUnavailable), with no binding active.
